title: windows11 系统中键盘映射有bug
author: yimmr

status.label: Expected Win+L remap behavior
status.detail: The reported Ctrl/Windows key swap turns Ctrl+L into the protected Win+L shortcut. Current Keyboard Manager source intentionally rejects Win+L mappings.

next_action: If Ctrl+L must remain an application shortcut, remove the Ctrl-to-Win direction of the swap; do not propose a product fix for the resulting Win+L behavior.

judgment.rationale: The reporter's configuration swaps Ctrl and Win, so pressing Ctrl+L after the swap produces Win+L. Current main explicitly classifies Win+L and chords containing Win+L as illegal shortcuts; this is a deliberate guard for the Windows lock-screen shortcut, not an unexplained fallback. The reporter's desired exception would require different mapping semantics than the configured global swap.
evidence: The Chinese report says the Windows and Ctrl key positions are swapped; Ctrl+L then becomes Win+L and locks the screen.
A later commenter asks to disable Win+L and says the registry DisabledHotkeys setting did not work.
At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardManagerEditorLibrary/EditorHelpers.cpp:137-145 rejects Win+L and any chord involving it.
At the same revision, KeyboardManagerEditorTest/EditorHelpersTests.cpp:302-318 verifies Win+L and Win+L chords are rejected while Ctrl+L remains a valid shortcut.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat the lock-screen shortcut as the expected result of mapping Ctrl to Win. If the reporter wants Ctrl+L to stay unchanged, use a one-way mapping that leaves Ctrl unmapped rather than swapping Ctrl and Win.

fix_assessment.rationale: The configured global swap intentionally maps Ctrl+L to Win+L, and Keyboard Manager already rejects attempts to define Win+L mappings. The requested behavior is a mapping exception/configuration change, not a defect in the current shortcut handler.

issue_context.summary: The reporter swaps the Windows and Ctrl keys and says Ctrl+L then becomes Win+L, which locks the screen.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.78.0 from the Microsoft Store.
The reporter's mapping swaps the Windows and Ctrl key positions; Ctrl+L consequently invokes Win+L.
A later commenter asks to disable Win+L and says the registry DisabledHotkeys setting did not help.
Current main rejects Win+L and chords containing Win+L in EditorHelpers::IsShortcutIllegal; unit tests also verify Ctrl+L remains a valid shortcut.
inferences: The reporter's expected behavior would require Ctrl+L to bypass the configured Ctrl-to-Win mapping, rather than applying the global swap consistently.
issue_context.analysis: The symptom follows directly from the requested key swap: Ctrl is configured to act as Win, so Ctrl+L becomes the Windows lock shortcut Win+L. Keyboard Manager intentionally prevents users from mapping that protected shortcut itself. If the desired behavior is to retain Ctrl+L for applications, a one-way Win-to-Ctrl mapping is the available configuration direction; no code change is supported by this report.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and its Chinese follow-up; no current reproduction or issue-specific configuration change was supplied.
Inspected current upstream main at 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769: EditorHelpers.cpp:137-145 and EditorHelpersTests.cpp:302-318.
No linked pull request or duplicate covering this report was found.
